headline: Investment income cushions weaker underwriting results
summary_short: CNA's Q2 2026 net income rose 7% y/y to $321M ($1.18 diluted EPS) as net investment losses shrank to $3M from $36M, while core income fell to $324M from $335M on a P&C combined ratio that widened to 96.5% from 94.1%.
summary_long: Net income rose 7% y/y to $321M ($1.18 diluted EPS) as net investment losses shrank to $3M from $36M, even as core income fell to $324M from $335M. P&C core income declined to $426M as the combined ratio widened to 96.5% from 94.1% (underlying combined ratio 94.2% vs 91.7%) on higher loss ratios across segments, despite net investment income rising to $461M. Net written premiums grew 4% on record new business of $718M. Corporate & Other's core loss narrowed to $92M from $114M despite a $77M after-tax legacy mass-tort charge. Net investment income overall rose to $701M on higher limited-partnership and fixed-income returns. Stockholders' equity was $11.2B; the board declared a $0.48/share dividend. No numeric forward guidance was given.
